survey: A handheld pocket calculator shown as a floating icon, tilted about 20° clockwise and seen from the front with slight perspective, on a yellow background with a pi-symbol pattern. Main parts: (1) A navy rounded-rectangle body with thick bevelled edges. Its back is not visible, and a floating icon needs no support. (2) A red four-cell solar strip set into the top edge above the display. (3) A light-grey LCD display window in a raised white bezel, set into the upper body and spanning most of its width. It is blank, which is a fair simplification. (4) A 4×4 keypad: twelve dark-blue square keys in three columns, and a right-hand column of four cyan keys that reads as the operator keys. Every key is a raised rounded square sitting in the body face with even spacing and a gap to the edge. The rows and columns follow the tilt and perspective of the body. Keys have no labels, which is an acceptable simplification. Counts add up: 1 display, 1 solar strip, 16 keys in a regular grid. Nothing passes through or melts into anything else, there are no loose parts and no invented parts. The keys could be pressed and the display could be read.
